gen.title: How an amendment moves from proposal to ratification

steps.label: Congress proposes amendment
steps.quote: The Constitution provides that an amendment may be proposed either by the Congress with a two-thirds majority vote

steps.label: Proposal offered as joint resolution
steps.quote: The Congress proposes an amendment in the form of a joint resolution.

steps.label: Archivist notifies governors
steps.quote: The Archivist submits the proposed amendment to the States for their consideration by sending a letter of notification to each Governor

steps.label: States return ratification records
steps.quote: When a State ratifies a proposed amendment, it sends the Archivist an original or certified copy of the State action

steps.label: Officials examine ratification documents
steps.quote: The OFR examines ratification documents for facial legal sufficiency and an authenticating signature.

steps.label: Amendment becomes part of Constitution
steps.quote: A proposed amendment becomes part of the Constitution as soon as it is ratified by three-fourths of the States (38 of 50 States).
